flows.name: On session start
flows.desc: Runs when a CLI session starts and after a compaction: the merged kernel, then the communication core (the ai-communication index and rules 0-8). KH cuts the answer into parts under the CLI's 10k cap.

args.head: COMMUNICATION CORE (ai-communication: the index tells which row fits a situation; rules 0-8 always apply to text you write for people):

flows.description: Runs when a CLI session starts and after a compaction: the merged kernel, then the communication core (the ai-communication index and rules 0-8). KH cuts the answer into parts under the CLI's 10k cap.

flows.name: On prompt submit
flows.desc: Runs for every prompt: masks secrets, finds the space, new messages, the prompt hook rules, the turn context, then names the nearest task flow.
flows.description: Runs for every prompt: masks secrets, finds the space, new messages, the prompt hook rules, the turn context, then names the nearest task flow.

flows.name: Before a tool runs
flows.desc: Runs before a guarded tool or a KH write: the rules that guard the tool (ask / deny), and for a KH write the write check rules.

input.kh_write: true when the call writes to KH

flows.description: Runs before a guarded tool or a KH write: the rules that guard the tool (ask / deny), and for a KH write the write check rules.

flows.name: When a turn stops
flows.desc: Runs when a turn changed something and stored no work log (kh-helper checks the transcript first): the reminder that blocks the stop; when the turn used a task map, the chain is remembered as a case and every row opened after the map that the map did not show becomes a gap event.
flows.description: Runs when a turn changed something and stored no work log (kh-helper checks the transcript first): the reminder that blocks the stop; when the turn used a task map, the chain is remembered as a case and every row opened after the map that the map did not show becomes a gap event.

flows.name: Load Kernel
flows.desc: The merged kernel: common rules, the profile's rules, the space's rules and the profile's untagged rules, rendered in the kernel's own order.
flows.description: The merged kernel: common rules, the profile's rules, the space's rules and the profile's untagged rules, rendered in the kernel's own order.

flows.name: Kernel Merge
flows.desc: The kernel's rules of three tiers merged per slot (project > personal > common, a locked common rule wins) and rendered in the kernel's order.

input.project: the space whose rules apply ('' = none)

args.from: Common Tier, Project Tier, Personal Tier

args.columns:
o1 = pl.when(pl.col("c_position").is_not_null()).then(pl.col("c_position")).otherwise(pl.col("position") + 1000)
o2 = pl.when(pl.col("kind") == "common").then(0).when(pl.col("kind") == "personal").then(1).otherwise(2)
block = pl.when(pl.col("kind") == "common").then(pl.col("text")).when(pl.col("overrides").fill_null("") != "").then(pl.concat_str([pl.lit("["), pl.col("kind"), pl.lit(", replaces the common rule '"), pl.col("overrides"), pl.lit("'] "), pl.col("text")])).otherwise(None)
extra = pl.when((pl.col("kind") != "common") & (pl.col("overrides").fill_null("") == "")).then(pl.concat_str([pl.lit("- "), pl.col("text")])).otherwise(None)

args.head: PERSONAL AND PROJECT RULES (already merged with the rules above; on overlap they win):

flows.description: The kernel's rules of three tiers merged per slot (project > personal > common, a locked common rule wins) and rendered in the kernel's order.

flows.name: Message Inbox
flows.desc: The notices the caller gets now: direct, announcements, mentions in the session's space, each once per account (or per session), as data.

args.columns:
live = (pl.col("expires_at") == "") | (pl.col("expires_at") > pl.col("now"))
in_project = (pl.col("channel") != "project") | ((pl.col("project") == pl.lit(input.get("project") or "")) & (pl.col("may_read") == True))
reaches = ((pl.col("to_actor") == "") | (pl.col("to_actor") == pl.col("actor"))) & ((pl.col("sender") != pl.col("reader")) | ((pl.col("actor") != "") & (pl.col("sender_actor") != "") & (pl.col("actor") != pl.col("sender_actor"))) | (((pl.col("actor") == "") | (pl.col("sender_actor") == "")) & (pl.col("channel") == "direct")))
per_account = pl.col("channel").is_in(["direct", "project"]) & (pl.col("to_actor") == "")
delivered = (pl.col("key_had") == True) | (pl.col("per_account") & (pl.col("account_had") == True)) | (~pl.col("per_account") & (pl.col("to_actor") == "") & (pl.col("first_seen") != "") & (pl.col("account_had") == True) & (pl.col("created_at") < pl.col("first_seen")))

flows.description: The notices the caller gets now: direct, announcements, mentions in the session's space, each once per account (or per session), as data.

flows.name: Save knowledge (split by the agent)
flows.desc: Splits a text to keep into nodes with keys, verbatim core facts and links, and saves them through the write core (check, match, upsert).

input.text: the knowledge, in the person's words
input.space: the space (empty: the session's bound one)

args.task:
Split this ${input.kind} into the write core's nodes (one node per fact or rule; topic ${input.topic}). Keep the person's words: every core line is quoted from the text.

{input.text}
args.guide: Node: {type, name, summary (one line), where, keys, core (<= 3 quotes, each a sentence of the text word for word, under 120 characters), sections: {detail: the whole text}}; edges: [[from, kind, to]] with ids of the bundle or qualified ids of rows the text names.

flows.description: Splits a text to keep into nodes with keys, verbatim core facts and links, and saves them through the write core (check, match, upsert).

flows.name: Promote a branch to prod
flows.desc: Owner only: the branch's rows of a scope (or the ids given) into prod, conflicts merged by the agent, the branch versions marked promoted.

input.ids: optional: only these logical ids (a list)

args.drop: variant, deleted, stored_id, stored_qid, qid, space, scope, ts, score, count, total, truncated, has_more

args.task: Prod changed these rows after the branch ${input.branch} read them. Merge each: keep prod's facts and the branch's change. Conflicts: ${steps.write.items}
args.guide: One item per row: {id, text, fields (optional), if: <the 'current' ts of the conflict>}.

flows.description: Owner only: the branch's rows of a scope (or the ids given) into prod, conflicts merged by the agent, the branch versions marked promoted.

flows.name: Turn Context
flows.desc: What the agent gets with each prompt about the space it is on: today's turn context (project, actions, findings, lessons), then the space's About and open findings.
flows.description: What the agent gets with each prompt about the space it is on: today's turn context (project, actions, findings, lessons), then the space's About and open findings.

flows.name: Guard the Tool
flows.desc: The space's and the profile's rules that guard the tool about to run: deny when one denies, else ask; nothing when no rule guards it.

args.cond: ((steps["Space Guards"].height > 0) and (steps["Space Guards"]["guard_decision"] == "deny").any()) or ((steps["Profile Guards"].height > 0) and (steps["Profile Guards"]["guard_decision"] == "deny").any())

flows.description: The space's and the profile's rules that guard the tool about to run: deny when one denies, else ask; nothing when no rule guards it.

flows.name: Task context (full retrieve)
flows.desc: The task map: keys + meaning, grouped on links, walked <= 2 steps (never through a hub), best matches and learned links first; at most 4,000 characters of pointers on what the caller can read.

examples: what does KH know about this task
build the task map for this
find everything about this bug in the space
not: thanks, that is all for now
what can you, the assistant, do for me
store a work log for this session
send a message to my colleague

input.space: the space (optional: the session's bound one)
input.actions: the task's hidden actions, ';' between them, each named with the system it touches (kernel rule 2), e.g. 'sign in to SAP BTP; trigger the GitHub CD pipeline'

steps.name: Lessons of the Task and Actions

args.task: ragstoraged.ask: read the feature and code graph of this space in RAGStoraged project ${steps.space.fields.rs_project} for the task, and answer its hits
args.guide: project=${steps.space.fields.rs_project}; k=10; expand=1; the task is the prompt. By hand: run python -m ragstore ask ${steps.space.fields.rs_project} "<the task>" -k 10 in the RAGStoraged folder and answer each hit as {id: 'rs:<project>:<node id>', text: '<label> - <file>: <snippet>', score}. RAGStoraged missing or without that project on this machine: answer one item {id: 'rs:missing', text: '<why>'}, never an empty list.

args.text: The feature and code graph of this space live in RAGStoraged project ${steps.space.fields.rs_project}, outside KH: read them with kh_graph("<question>").

args.lead: Rows of a solved chain like this task, read fresh. Open a row with expand <id> if a detail is needed.

args.from: Keys in the Task, Meaning: Knowledge, Meaning: Findings, Meaning: Lessons

args.cond: (steps["Read RAGStoraged"].height + steps["Graph Pointer"].height + steps["Lessons of the Task and Actions"].height) > 0

args.message: nothing in what you can see; ask the user. KH has no row on this task in what you can read: do not guess.

args.lead: Several candidates match this task. Ask the user which one before acting.

args.from: Meaning: Knowledge, Meaning: Findings, Meaning: Lessons, Keys in the Task

args.lessons: Lessons of the Task and Actions

args.lead: Open with kh_expand(id) the rows you use. The map shows only the rows closest to the task: when the task has several steps, checks or rules, or asks for everything known, ALSO open each '+N ... under <id>' line with kh_expand(<id>), kh_expand('~more') for the next rows by meaning, before you answer; stop when a page adds nothing new.

grid: Lessons of the Task and Actions

flows.name: Plan the actions
flows.desc: Entry layer: the LLM sends the actions it detected in the prompt; none sent means talk with user. Plans for each action, then the task map when there is a specific task.

input.actions: the actions detected in the prompt (empty = talk with user)
input.space: the space (optional: the session's bound one)

args.lead: Talk with the user: follow the plan and the communication rules.
Plans for each action, then the task map. Follow the plans; act on the map.

flows.description: Entry layer: the LLM sends the actions it detected in the prompt; none sent means talk with user. Plans for each action, then the task map when there is a specific task.

flows.name: Save structured (shared core)
flows.desc: The one place the save rules live: check the bundle, match it to what exists, save nodes and links with the access of their sources. Run by the other save flows; input {space, bundle}.

input.lessons_status: optional: the status every lesson node gets (a retro: proposed)

args.message: Some nodes break the save rules: ${steps.check.fields.reasons}. Fix them with the reasons given and hand the bundle in again; nothing was saved.

flows.description: The one place the save rules live: check the bundle, match it to what exists, save nodes and links with the access of their sources. Run by the other save flows; input {space, bundle}.

flows.name: Save a retro (S2)
flows.desc: Turns a finished task (the newest case of this session, or input.case_id) into findings, fixes and lessons linked to the rows it used, and records what its map missed as gap events. Lessons start proposed.

input.space: the space (empty: the session's bound one)
input.case_id: optional: the case to look back on

args.message: No case to look back on

args.task: Look back on case ${steps.case.items.0.qid} (task: ${steps.case.items.0.text}). From the chain and its rows, write the finding (symptom + cause), the fix and the lesson (the rule for next time) as nodes linked to the rows of the chain. Quote the core word for word from a src row; do not reword. Lessons start as proposed.
args.guide: Node: {type, name, summary (one line), where, keys, core (<= 3 quotes), src: [{row: <qid>, quote}]}; edges: [[from, kind, to]] with ids of the bundle or rows of the chain.

args.task: List what the map of case ${steps.case.items.0.qid} did not show but the work needed: the rows you opened later, or the raw row that held a fact. An empty list is fine.
args.guide: Each gap: {found: <the map's leading row id>, holder: <the row that held it> | src_row: <the raw row>, why}

args.lead: Retro saved: lessons proposed (trusted once a human approves or a later task confirms them), gaps queued for the distiller.

flows.description: Turns a finished task (the newest case of this session, or input.case_id) into findings, fixes and lessons linked to the rows it used, and records what its map missed as gap events. Lessons start proposed.

flows.name: Distil at night (S3)
flows.desc: The distiller (maintainers): open gaps become learned links (the gap closes in the same call) or new nodes; then the learned-link growth guards (remove contradicted, decay, consolidate to the parent, evict over the cap, flag strict promotion), levels and extractive summaries, and a Quality Report row in the space's logs. KH does not fire the 02:00 trigger yet: run it by name.

args.task:
For each open gap, name the row that holds the missing fact and link it learned from the map's leading row (from = found[0], to = the holder). Cut a new node only when no row holds it (quote its core from the src row). Gaps:
${steps.gaps.fields.list}
args.guide: links: [{gap_id, from, to}]; new_nodes: nodes of the write core (type, name, summary, where, keys, core <= 3 quotes, src [{row, quote}]).

args.task: Rebuild the summary node of every feature or module whose rows changed: extractive quotes and child counts only, never paraphrased, never quoting a row of narrower access.

args.text: QUALITY REPORT ${input.space}: open gaps ${steps.gaps.fields.count}; learned links ${steps.learn.fields.linked}, gaps closed ${steps.learn.fields.closed}; ${steps.housekeep.fields.text}; ${steps.levels.fields.text}

flows.description: The distiller (maintainers): open gaps become learned links (the gap closes in the same call) or new nodes; then the learned-link growth guards (remove contradicted, decay, consolidate to the parent, evict over the cap, flag strict promotion), levels and extractive summaries, and a Quality Report row in the space's logs. KH does not fire the 02:00 trigger yet: run it by name.

flows.name: Save a spec (S1)
flows.desc: A person hands in a spec: the raw text is kept as the source, the agent outlines and splits it into nodes, KH checks and matches them, the person approves a preview, then the shared core saves it.

examples: put this functional spec into KH
store this specification in the space
import this requirements document with its modules, features and steps
here is the functional specification of the feature, save it
not: store what we learned as a lesson

input.space: the space (optional: the session's bound one)

args.task: Pass 1, outline: list the modules and features the spec defines; match each to a row of the space or mark it new. The raw spec is row ${steps.raw.fields.new_row_id}.
args.guide: [{name, type module|feature, parent, same_as id|null, source span}]

args.task: Pass 2, for each feature of the outline: its steps, UI texts, APIs, tables, settings, rules and owners as nodes with links; quote rules word for word from the raw spec row ${steps.raw.fields.new_row_id}.
args.guide: Node: {type, name, summary, where, keys, core <= 3 quotes, src [{row, quote}]}; edges [[from, kind, to]].

args.task: Show the person a preview: how many nodes are new, how many update a row, which matches are unsure, which nodes failed the check. Ask them to save.

args.lead: The spec is saved: the raw spec plus nodes and links.

args.message: Nothing saved except the raw spec

flows.description: A person hands in a spec: the raw text is kept as the source, the agent outlines and splits it into nodes, KH checks and matches them, the person approves a preview, then the shared core saves it.

flows.name: Save a work log
flows.desc: Writes a work log row into the hot log window of its space, then moves the oldest hot log rows over the limit into the logs of the space each belongs to (ids kept, never lost). kh_log (POST /vector/add scope log) runs it after storing the row; an agent can run it by name.

input.space: the space (empty: the session's bound one)
input.row_id: set by kh_log: the row is stored

args.columns:
live = ~((pl.col("max_age_days") > 0) & (pl.col("ts") > 0) & ((pl.col("now") - pl.col("ts")) / 86400 > pl.col("max_age_days")))
live_ts = pl.when(pl.col("live")).then(pl.col("ts")).otherwise(None)
slot_pos = pl.col("live_ts").rank("ordinal", descending=True).over("space")
slot_newest = pl.col("live_ts").max().over("space")
slot_rank = pl.col("slot_newest").rank("dense", descending=True)

args.text: log row ${input.row_id}${steps.write.fields.new_row_id} saved; moved ${steps.move.fields.moved} hot log rows to the logs of their space

flows.description: Writes a work log row into the hot log window of its space, then moves the oldest hot log rows over the limit into the logs of the space each belongs to (ids kept, never lost). kh_log (POST /vector/add scope log) runs it after storing the row; an agent can run it by name.
